semanticText:
# Activation Clause

Maintains one party roster, a shared acceptance boundary and an access guard for the executing document. It separates agreement to terms from the ability to read participant timelines. Hosted bootstrap resolves account locators into authenticated transports before initialization. Executable hooks come from the admitted exact clause type.

## Configuration

Configuration is supplied through `parameters`; runtime functions read `/clauses/activation/parameters` and maintain `/activation` in the same document.

- `parties` must be a nonempty object keyed by party role. Each party needs `lead/channel`; additional `representatives` are keyed by representative name. Party and representative keys must be nonempty text without `.`, `/`, `~` or `__`. Lead channels use the party role; additional transports use `party__representative`. Party and representative names and business descriptions identify participants but do not prove authority.
- `required` identifies the party leads whose acceptance is needed. It defaults to all initial party keys. `revision` defaults to `1`. An explicitly empty `required` list removes the approval requirement, but cannot be used with enabled negotiation.
- `allowNewParties` defaults to `false`. `frozen` defaults to `false`; an existing `/partyRosterFrozen` value of `true` also freezes party management during planning. Freezing the roster is distinct from closing the document.
- `accessPaths` defaults to `[]` and names embedded Timeline Access documents. `readers` defaults to `{}` and supplies additional groups of alternative reader keys. Each party's `readerKeys` supplies its lead group; each additional representative's `readerKeys` supplies that transport's group. These roster groups replace same-named entries in `readers`.
- `preActivationOperations` and `preActivationChannels` default to `[]`. They allow specified external operations and nonexternal channel deliveries before acceptance, subject to the access and closure checks below. Generated approval, party-update and negotiation operations receive this exception automatically.
- `negotiation/allowedPaths` defaults to `[]`; a nonempty list enables negotiation. Paths must be unique absolute paths with nonempty segments and no `~`. They cannot enter `clauses`, `contracts`, `activation`, `clauseRuntime`, `type`, `name` or `description`, or equal or descend from a configured access path. Selected fields must exist and be text, integer, double or Boolean. Negotiation also requires a document `type` and at least one required approver.
- `admission/approvers` must be nonempty for the supplied approved-admission helper to admit parties.

## Access and activation

For each `Timeline Channel` transport, one embedded Timeline Access document must name the exact timeline, match its provider and include at least one key from **every** reader group. Keys within a group are alternatives. Coverage split across multiple access documents does not satisfy this single-document test for a transport. Transports descending from `External Channel` are exempt from this Timeline Access check; other channel kinds are rejected.

Embedded access histories remain provider-owned. Installing one validates its native executable policy, initialization and provider checkpoint; installation does not grant access. Public access-update deliveries remain available while private access is unavailable. Access notifications prompt a refresh; executed permission state and authenticated history establish the permission facts.

`accessReady` and `functional` hold the same access-test result. This test includes proposed parties from access requests whose `expectedRevision` still matches the activation revision. `termsAccepted` requires every role in `required` to have a true entry in `approved`, and every agreed `terms.fields` value to match the corresponding document field. `active` additionally requires access readiness and that `closed` is not true.

The maintained `status` distinguishes:

- `WAITING_FOR_ACCESS`: access is missing before any recorded activation; permission updates are awaited.
- `SUSPENDED_ACCESS`: access is missing after an earlier activation; restored permission coverage is awaited.
- `AWAITING_ACCEPTANCE`: access is ready, but required lead approvals or agreement with the recorded terms is missing.
- `ACTIVE`: access and acceptance conditions are satisfied and the document is not closed.
- `CLOSED`: `closed` is true, taking precedence over the other statuses.

`reason` reports `PARTICIPANT_ACCESS_MISSING`, otherwise `ACCEPTANCE_REQUIRED`, otherwise an empty string; it is not a separate closure indicator. `everActivated` remembers whether an active state has ever been committed and remains true through later suspension.

`Clauses Initialized`, relevant embedded `Timeline Access Updated` events and party-addition handling trigger refreshes. `Document Activated` marks the first committed activation. `Document Access Suspended` is emitted when an active document loses access. `Document Access Restored` requires the document to become active again after missing access; restored access alone can still leave acceptance outstanding.

The dispatch policy permits initialization and registered embedded access updates through its activation gate. Other deliveries require initialized activation state, recorded `accessReady`, a fresh access check and an open document. Pre-activation exceptions and narrowly validated admission-consent registrations can then pass before acceptance; remaining work requires business readiness. Other installed policies still apply. A denied external input is consumed and checkpointed, not deferred for automatic execution after activation.

## Acceptance and party changes

`approve_<party>` is callable through that party's lead channel. It requires `call/requireExactDocumentVersion=true`, the current `revision`, and complete participant access. With negotiation enabled, it also requires the current `termsRef`. A newly recorded approval emits `Terms Accepted`; repeating an existing approval returns successfully without another acceptance event. One party's acceptance does not establish that all activation conditions are satisfied.

`updateParty_<party>` also requires exact-document review and a current party lead, with an unfrozen roster. Its optional `party` defaults to the invoking party. An existing party may manage only itself; adding another party requires an explicit new key and `allowNewParties=true`. `replacement` needs `lead/channel`, valid representative names and access coverage for the resulting roster. Contract-name conflicts are rejected. No revision argument is required. A successful update advances the activation revision, clears all approvals and emits `Party Changed`; a newly added party is also appended to `required`.

`Party Addition Requested` is a separate admission route. Stale revisions and already-recorded requests are ignored. Supplied access documents are validated and embedded, and missing coverage can emit `Party Access Update Requested` for individual existing-party transports. Such an event requests an owner-controlled access change; it is neither permission evidence nor participant consent. Its readiness check covers every transport of the parent party.

The approved-admission helper requires an unfrozen roster, matching `expectedRevision`, a nonempty admission policy, compatible existing main identities and complete access. Main-identity comparison uses the exact lead channel and the same nonempty, duplicate-free set of primary reader keys. This helper advances the revision when it adds parties, but does not automatically add them to `required` or consent for them.

## Negotiated terms

Initialization records agreed scalar values in `terms.fields` and identifies their fixed document context in `terms.definition`; `terms.ref` identifies that combination. The initial identity excludes configured access documents, `accessPaths`, `readers` and party-level `readerKeys`. `termsRevision` and the negotiation revision start at `1`; proposal, history and outcome maps start empty, and `negotiation.editable` starts true when term initialization runs. Missing runtime fields do not themselves establish these defaults.

With negotiation enabled, each required lead receives `proposeChanges`, `proposeAndActivate`, `activate`, `withdrawProposal`, `rejectProposal` and `withdrawAcceptance` operations, suffixed by its role. These require exact-document review and a caller in `required`.

`proposeChanges` requires the current `baseTermsRef`, a nonempty list of `changes`, and a unique nonempty `proposalId` containing neither `/` nor `~`. Each change has an allowed `path` and a `replacement` of the current field's primitive kind. Duplicate paths, unchanged resulting terms and candidates that fail the document's type are rejected. Reusing a pending identifier is accepted only for the same proposal content and revision. Replacing a different pending proposal requires its identifier in `supersedes`; the old proposal closes as `SUPERSEDED`. Recording an offer emits `Amendment Proposed` without applying it.

`activate` selects either current terms or a pending offer. Current terms require `termsRef` and no `proposalId`, and use the ordinary approval path. Proposed terms require both the matching `proposalId` and `termsRef`; the stored base reference, field set, candidate validity and terms identity are rechecked. Approval is recorded for the caller. Only unanimous required-lead approval applies the offer, emits `Amendment Applied`, advances both activation and terms revisions, transfers proposal approvals into `approved`, closes the proposal as `APPLIED` and freezes negotiation. `proposeAndActivate` proposes and records the caller's acceptance; its name does not guarantee unanimous acceptance or activation.

Before first activation, a required lead may withdraw its acceptance of the selected current or proposed terms. Only the proposer may withdraw an offer; any required lead may reject it. These close offers as `WITHDRAWN` or `REJECTED`. Once `everActivated` is true, proposal creation, proposal withdrawal/rejection and acceptance withdrawal are closed, including during access suspension.

Roster or required-list changes renew the terms identity and advance `termsRevision`; a pending offer closes as `AUTHORITY_CHANGED`. With negotiation enabled, these changes also clear current approvals. Activation through ordinary current-term approval supersedes any pending offer and freezes negotiation. Proposal `history` records closure, including rejected and withdrawn offers; it is not proof of application.

Before first activation with negotiation enabled, clause-set changes are locked. Direct replacement of this activation clause is rejected in favor of its party operations. Operation availability describes a callable mechanism, not a personal obligation or the current reader's permission.
